Select the reagents that reduce nitriles to primary amines :
A. (i) $\text{LiAlH}_4$; (ii) $\text{H}_2\text{O}$
B. $\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}$
C. $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$
D. $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$
E. $\text{Br}_2/\text{aq. NaOH}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Nitriles ($R-CN$) can be reduced to primary amines ($R-CH_2NH_2$) using strong reducing agents or catalytic hydrogenation.

Reagent A: $\text{LiAlH}_4$ followed by hydrolysis is a strong reducing agent that reduces nitriles to primary amines.

Reagent C: $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$ (catalytic hydrogenation) reduces nitriles to primary amines.

Reagent D: $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ (Mendius reduction) provides nascent hydrogen and reduces nitriles to primary amines.

Reagent B: $\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}$ is typically used to reduce nitro compounds to amines. (Note: $\text{SnCl}_2 + \text{HCl}$ is used in Stephen reduction to convert nitriles to aldehydes).

Reagent E: $\text{Br}_2/\text{aq. NaOH}$ is used for Hoffmann bromamide degradation to convert amides to primary amines, not nitriles.

Thus, A, C, and D are the correct reagents.

Answer: A, C and D only

Identify the reactions which give aniline as the major product.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
Let us analyze each reaction to determine the major product:

Reaction A: Benzonitrile ($C_6H_5CN$) is reduced by $LiAlH_4$, a strong reducing agent, to form benzylamine.
$C_6H_5CN \xrightarrow{LiAlH_4} C_6H_5CH_2NH_2$

Reaction B: Benzamide ($C_6H_5CONH_2$) undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation in the presence of $KOH$ and $Br_2$ to form aniline.
$C_6H_5CONH_2 \xrightarrow{KOH, Br_2} C_6H_5NH_2$

Reaction C: Nitrobenzene ($C_6H_5NO_2$) is not reduced to aniline by $NaBH_4$. $NaBH_4$ is a mild reducing agent and generally does not reduce the $-NO_2$ group.

Reaction D: Acetanilide ($C_6H_5NHCOCH_3$) undergoes acid-catalyzed hydrolysis upon heating to yield aniline and acetic acid.
$C_6H_5NHCOCH_3 \xrightarrow{HCl, H_2O, \Delta} C_6H_5NH_2 + CH_3COOH$

Thus, reactions B and D give aniline as the major product.

Answer: B and D only

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow[\text{UV light}]{\text{Cl}_2} X \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_3} Y \xrightarrow[(\text{monochlorinated product})]{\text{(i) NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}\ \ \text{(ii) H}_2\text{O}} Z$

Ethane undergoes free radical halogenation with chlorine in the presence of UV light to form ethyl chloride (X).

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 + \text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV light}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} \ (X)$

Ethylamine, being a primary aliphatic amine, reacts with nitrous acid ($\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}$) to form an unstable aliphatic diazonium salt, which decomposes to yield a carbocation. The carbocation reacts with water to form ethanol (Z).

Answer: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is more basic than aniline?
questions.solution:
Benzyl amine is more basic than aniline because the benzyl group is an electron-donating group on account of the + I effect. So, it is capable of increasing the electron density of $\mathrm{N}$ of the $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ group. Thus, because of the higher electron density, the rate of donation of a free pair of electrons is increased, i.e., the basic character is higher. Phenyl and nitro groups are electron attractive groups, so they are able to decrease the electron density of $\mathrm{N}$ of $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ group. Hence, they are less basic than aniline.
A Caution Benzylamine has localised lone pair therefore it is more basic.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact explanation for the assertion. Read the following statements regarding the electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions of aniline:

(B) Direct nitration yields a significant amount of $m$-nitroaniline.
(C) The anilinium ion formed in strongly acidic medium is an activating group.
(D) Monobromination requires protection of the $-\text{NH}_2$ group by acetylation.

Statement (A) is correct: Aniline forms a salt with the Lewis acid catalyst ($\text{AlCl}_3$), which acts as a strongly deactivating group, preventing Friedel-Crafts reactions.

Statement (B) is correct: During direct nitration in a strongly acidic medium, aniline is protonated to form the anilinium ion, which directs the incoming electrophile to the meta position, yielding about 47% $m$-nitroaniline.

Statement (C) is incorrect: The anilinium ion ($-\text{NH}_3^+$) is a strongly deactivating group, not an activating group.

Statement (D) is correct: The $-\text{NH}_2$ group is highly activating, leading to tribromination (2,4,6-tribromoaniline) upon direct reaction with bromine water. To obtain the monobromo derivative, the $-\text{NH}_2$ group must first be protected by acetylation to reduce its activating effect.

Therefore, statements (A), (B) and (D) are correct.

Answer: (A), (B) and (D) only

In Flask X, at $273-278\text{ K}$, aniline reacts with nitrous acid (generated in situ from $\text{NaNO}_2$ and dilute $\text{HCl}$) to undergo stable diazotization, forming benzenediazonium chloride as the major product.

The conversion of chloroethane (2 carbon atoms) to propan-1-amine (3 carbon atoms) involves an ascent of the amine series, which requires the addition of one carbon atom.

Treatment of chloroethane with alcoholic $\text{KCN}$ (Reagent A) results in nucleophilic substitution to form propanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$) as the major product (Intermediate X).
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Cl} + \text{KCN (alc.)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{KCl}$

The reduction of propanenitrile to propan-1-amine requires a strong reducing agent such as $\text{LiAlH}_4$, $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$, or $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ (Reagent B).

If $\text{AgCN}$ were used, ethyl isocyanide would form, which upon reduction gives a secondary amine (N-methylethanamine). Reagents like $\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}$ are used for nitro compounds, and $\text{Br}_2/\text{NaOH}$ is used for amides, neither of which will reduce a nitrile to a primary amine.

Answer: A = alc. $\text{KCN}$, B = $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$

Assertion (A): N-methylaniline reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to yield a product that is insoluble in aqueous NaOH.
Reason (R): The sulphonamide formed by the reaction of a secondary amine with Hinsberg's reagent lacks an acidic hydrogen atom.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
N-methylaniline ($C_6H_5NHCH_3$) is a secondary ($2^{\circ}$) amine.

It reacts with Hinsberg's reagent (benzenesulphonyl chloride, $C_6H_5SO_2Cl$) to form N-methyl-N-phenylbenzenesulphonamide.

Because there is no hydrogen atom attached to the nitrogen in this sulphonamide, it lacks an acidic hydrogen. Therefore, it is insoluble in aqueous alkali (NaOH).

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Aniline reacts with nitrous acid at $273-278\text{ K}$ to yield a stable diazonium salt, while ethylamine yields ethanol and nitrogen gas under identical conditions.
Reason (R): The stability of the benzene diazonium ion at low temperatures is due to the strong $+I$ effect of the phenyl ring.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because primary aromatic amines like aniline react with nitrous acid at $273-278\text{ K}$ to form arenediazonium salts which are stable at this low temperature. Primary aliphatic amines like ethylamine react under the same conditions to form highly unstable alkyl diazonium salts, which immediately decompose to yield alcohols (ethanol) and nitrogen gas.

Reason (R) is incorrect because the stability of the benzene diazonium ion is due to resonance stabilization (the delocalization of the positive charge over the benzene ring), not the $+I$ effect. The phenyl ring actually exerts an electron-withdrawing $-I$ effect.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Fluorobenzene is prepared by heating dry benzenediazonium fluoroborate rather than benzenediazonium chloride.

Reason (R): Benzenediazonium fluoroborate is water insoluble and stable in the dry state at room temperature, whereas the chloride salt decomposes easily in the dry state.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: Fluorobenzene is prepared by the Balz-Schiemann reaction, which involves heating dry benzenediazonium fluoroborate.

Reason (R) is true: According to NCERT, benzenediazonium fluoroborate is water insoluble and stable at room temperature. This allows it to be precipitated, filtered, dried, and safely heated. In contrast, benzenediazonium chloride is soluble in water and decomposes easily in the dry state, making it unsafe and impractical to isolate and heat dry.

Therefore, the stability and insolubility of the fluoroborate salt is the exact reason it is chosen for this preparation. Thus, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of amines can be successfully prepared using Gabriel phthalimide synthesis?
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is exclusively used for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines.

It cannot be used to prepare primary aromatic amines because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion. It is also not applicable for the preparation of secondary or tertiary amines.

Aniline and $p$-toluidine are primary aromatic amines, hence they cannot be prepared by this method.

N-Methylethanamine is a secondary amine and N,N-Dimethylamine is a tertiary amine, so they cannot be prepared either.

Benzylamine ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$) is a primary aliphatic amine because the $-\text{NH}_2$ group is attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon, not directly to the benzene ring. Ethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$) is also a primary aliphatic amine. Therefore, both benzylamine and ethanamine can be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.

Answer: Benzylamine and Ethanamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following amides will yield aniline when treated with bromine and aqueous potassium hydroxide?
questions.solution:
The reaction of an amide with bromine and aqueous potassium hydroxide is the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction.

In this reaction, a primary amide ($R-CONH_2$) is converted into a primary amine ($R-NH_2$) containing one carbon atom less than the parent amide. The carbonyl carbon of the amide is lost as a carbonate ion.

Since the product is aniline ($C_6H_5NH_2$), the starting amide must contain the phenyl group directly attached to the carbonyl carbon. Therefore, the starting amide is benzamide ($C_6H_5CONH_2$).

Phenylacetamide would yield benzylamine. N-Methylbenzamide and acetanilide are secondary amides and do not undergo this reaction to give primary amines.

Answer: Benzamide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following halogen compounds cannot be used as a starting material to prepare a primary amine via the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis?
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves the nucleophilic substitution ($\mathrm{S_N2}$) of an alkyl halide by the potassium salt of phthalimide (phthalimide anion).

Aryl halides, such as chlorobenzene, do not undergo nucleophilic substitution reactions easily under normal conditions. This is due to the partial double bond character of the $\mathrm{C-Cl}$ bond arising from resonance, and the $sp^2$ hybridised state of the carbon atom attached to the halogen.

Therefore, the phthalimide anion cannot displace the chloride ion from chlorobenzene, making it impossible to prepare aromatic primary amines by this method.

Benzyl chloride, 1-bromobutane, and 2-bromopropane are aliphatic or aralkyl halides that can readily undergo nucleophilic substitution to yield their respective primary amines.

Answer: Chlorobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Ethanamine is heated with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide to form an intermediate A. The intermediate A is then reduced using lithium aluminium hydride to form the major product B.

The IUPAC name of the major product B is:
questions.solution:
Ethanamine ($CH_3CH_2NH_2$), being a primary aliphatic amine, undergoes the carbylamine reaction when heated with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide. This produces ethyl isocyanide ($CH_3CH_2NC$) as intermediate A.

Reduction of ethyl isocyanide with lithium aluminium hydride ($LiAlH_4$) yields a secondary amine, N-methylethanamine ($CH_3CH_2NHCH_3$), as the major product B.

If the intermediate were incorrectly assumed to be a nitrile, it would reduce to propan-1-amine, but the carbylamine reaction specifically produces an isocyanide which reduces to a secondary amine.

Answer: N-Methylethanamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When N-ethylethanamine is treated with benzenesulphonyl chloride and the resulting mixture is shaken with aqueous NaOH, what is the expected observation?
options: A solid is formed which dissolves in aqueous NaOH.
No reaction occurs with benzenesulphonyl chloride.
A solid is formed which remains insoluble in aqueous NaOH.
A clear solution is formed immediately upon adding benzenesulphonyl chloride.
questions.solution:
N-ethylethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) is a secondary ($2^{\circ}$) amine.

Secondary amines react with Hinsberg's reagent (benzenesulphonyl chloride) to form N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamides.

Since N,N-diethylbenzenesulphonamide does not contain any hydrogen atom attached to the nitrogen atom, it is not acidic and therefore remains insoluble in aqueous alkali (NaOH).

Primary amines form a solid soluble in alkali, while tertiary amines do not react with Hinsberg's reagent to form stable sulphonamides.

Answer: A solid is formed which remains insoluble in aqueous NaOH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List IList II
(A) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis(I) Catalyst forms a deactivating salt with the substrate
(B) Friedel-Crafts alkylation of aniline(II) Yields an amine with one carbon less than the reactant
(C) Carbylamine reaction(III) Cannot be used to prepare primary aromatic amines
(D) Hoffmann bromamide degradation(IV) Used as a test for primary amines yielding a foul-smelling substance

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines. It cannot be used to prepare primary aromatic amines because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide. Thus, (A) matches with (III).

(B) Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation because the basic amino group reacts with the Lewis acid catalyst (like $\text{AlCl}_3$) to form a strongly deactivating salt. Thus, (B) matches with (I).

(C) Carbylamine reaction is given only by primary amines (aliphatic and aromatic), which on heating with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide form foul-smelling isocyanides or carbylamines. Thus, (C) matches with (IV).

(D) Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction involves the migration of an alkyl or aryl group from the carbonyl carbon of the amide to the nitrogen atom, yielding an amine with one carbon atom less than the parent amide. Thus, (D) matches with (II).

Answer: (A) - (III), (B) - (I), (C) - (IV), (D) - (II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are four statements regarding the chemistry of amines:
(I) Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction produces an amine with one carbon atom less than the parent amide.
(II) Carbylamine reaction is given by both aliphatic and aromatic primary amines.
(III) Reduction of alkyl isocyanides with $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ yields primary amines.
(IV) The product formed by the reaction of a secondary amine with Hinsberg's reagent is soluble in aqueous alkali.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct: In Hoffmann bromamide degradation, the amine formed contains one carbon less than the parent amide due to the migration of an alkyl or aryl group from the carbonyl carbon to the nitrogen atom.

Statement (II) is correct: Both aliphatic and aromatic primary amines on heating with chloroform and ethanolic $\mathrm{KOH}$ form foul-smelling isocyanides (carbylamine reaction).

Statement (III) is incorrect: Reduction of alkyl isocyanides ($\mathrm{R-NC}$) with $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ yields secondary amines ($\mathrm{R-NH-CH_3}$), whereas reduction of alkyl cyanides ($\mathrm{R-CN}$) yields primary amines.

Statement (IV) is incorrect: Secondary amines react with Hinsberg's reagent (benzenesulphonyl chloride) to form N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide. Since it does not have any hydrogen atom attached to the nitrogen atom, it is not acidic and is insoluble in aqueous alkali.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:

Phenylacetic acid $\xrightarrow[\Delta]{NH_3} A \xrightarrow{Br_2/NaOH} B$

The final product B is:
questions.solution:
Phenylacetic acid ($C_6H_5CH_2COOH$) reacts with ammonia to form an ammonium salt, which on strong heating loses a water molecule to form 2-phenylacetamide ($C_6H_5CH_2CONH_2$). This is intermediate A.

2-Phenylacetamide is treated with bromine and sodium hydroxide, which are the reagents for the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction.

In this reaction, the primary amide loses its carbonyl carbon to form a primary amine with one carbon atom less. Thus, the $-CONH_2$ group is converted to an $-NH_2$ group.

$C_6H_5CH_2CONH_2 \xrightarrow{Br_2/NaOH} C_6H_5CH_2NH_2$

The final product B is benzylamine.

Answer: Benzylamine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid to release nitrogen gas quantitatively.
Reason (R): Aliphatic diazonium salts are highly unstable and decompose to yield alcohols and nitrogen gas.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid (prepared in situ from $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$) to form aliphatic diazonium salts.

These aliphatic diazonium salts are highly unstable, even at low temperatures, and immediately decompose to liberate nitrogen gas quantitatively along with the formation of alcohols.

The quantitative evolution of nitrogen gas is practically used in the estimation of amino acids and proteins.

Thus, the Assertion (A) is a correct statement. The Reason (R) correctly states the instability and decomposition of the intermediate diazonium salt, which is the exact chemical cause for the quantitative release of nitrogen gas mentioned in the Assertion.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Reduction of benzonitrile and phenyl isocyanide with $LiAlH_4$ yields the same primary amine.

Reason (R): Benzonitrile and phenyl isocyanide are functional isomers containing the same number of carbon and nitrogen atoms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because the reduction of benzonitrile ($C_6H_5CN$) with $LiAlH_4$ yields benzylamine ($C_6H_5CH_2NH_2$), which is a primary amine, whereas the reduction of phenyl isocyanide ($C_6H_5NC$) yields N-methylaniline ($C_6H_5NHCH_3$), which is a secondary amine.

Reason (R) is true because benzonitrile and phenyl isocyanide both have the same molecular formula ($C_7H_5N$) but possess different functional groups ($-CN$ and $-NC$), making them functional isomers.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :

List I (Reaction)List II (Product Characteristics)
A. $\text{R}-\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}}$I. Secondary amine with a methyl group
B. $\text{R}-\text{NC} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4}$II. Primary amine with one carbon less than the substrate
C. $\text{R}-\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{aq. NaOH}}$III. Primary amine with the same number of carbon atoms as the substrate
D. $\text{R}-\text{NO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}}$IV. Primary amine formed by reduction of an oxygen-containing nitrogen compound

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Reaction A: Reduction of nitriles ($\text{R}-\text{CN}$) with $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ (Mendius reduction) yields a primary amine with the same number of carbon atoms as the starting nitrile. (A matches III)

Reaction B: Reduction of isonitriles ($\text{R}-\text{NC}$) with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields a secondary amine containing a methyl group ($\text{R}-\text{NH}-\text{CH}_3$). (B matches I)

Reaction C: Hoffmann bromamide degradation of amides ($\text{R}-\text{CONH}_2$) with $\text{Br}_2$ and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ produces a primary amine with one carbon atom less than the parent amide. (C matches II)

Reaction D: Reduction of nitro compounds ($\text{R}-\text{NO}_2$) with $\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}$ yields a primary amine. The substrate is an oxygen-containing nitrogen compound. (D matches IV)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Guanidine is a much stronger organic base than urea.

Reason (R): The conjugate acid of urea is stabilized by three equivalent resonance structures.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Guanidine is a very strong organic base because its conjugate acid (guanidinium ion) is highly stable due to three equivalent resonance structures. Urea is a very weak base because its nitrogen lone pairs are involved in resonance with the electronegative carbonyl oxygen, making them unavailable for protonation. Therefore, Assertion (A) is true.

Reason (R) is false because it is the conjugate acid of guanidine, not urea, that is stabilized by three equivalent resonance structures.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): N-methylethanamide on treatment with bromine and ethanolic sodium hydroxide gives N-methylmethanamine.
Reason (R): Hoffmann bromamide degradation is given only by primary amides.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
N-methylethanamide (C$H_3$CONHCH_3$) is a secondary amide. The Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction is a characteristic reaction of primary amides (R-CONH_2$) only. Secondary and tertiary amides do not undergo this reaction.

Therefore, N-methylethanamide will not undergo degradation with bromine and ethanolic sodium hydroxide to yield N-methylmethanamine. Thus, Assertion (A) is false.

Reason (R) correctly states that the reaction is specific to primary amides, which is a true statement.

Hence, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the major product $C$ formed in the following sequence of reactions:
$\text{Benzamide} \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{NaOH}} A \xrightarrow[\text{273-278 K}]{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} B \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O, warm}} C$
questions.solution:
Benzamide undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation with $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$ to form aniline ($A$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{NaOH}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \ (A)$

Aniline reacts with nitrous acid ($\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$) at 273-278 K to undergo diazotization, forming benzene diazonium chloride ($B$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow[\text{273-278 K}]{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^{+}\text{Cl}^{-} \ (B)$

Warming the stable aromatic diazonium salt with water hydrolyses it to yield phenol ($C$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^{+}\text{Cl}^{-} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O, warm}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} \ (C) + \text{N}_2 + \text{HCl}$

Thus, the major product $C$ is phenol.

Benzene diazonium chloride is the intermediate $B$, not the final product. Bromobenzene would be formed if the Sandmeyer reaction ($\text{Cu}_2\text{Br}_2/\text{HBr}$) was used. Benzyl alcohol is incorrect as the carbon skeleton has lost a carbon atom in the first step.

Answer: Phenol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List IList II
(A) Propan-2-amine(I) Hinsberg's reagent
(B) N-methylethanamine(II) Forms an alkali-insoluble solid with Hinsberg's reagent
(C) N,N-dimethylmethanamine(III) Does not react with Hinsberg's reagent to form a sulphonamide
(D) Benzenesulphonyl chloride(IV) Forms an alkali-soluble solid with Hinsberg's reagent


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Propan-2-amine ($CH_3CH(NH_2)CH_3$) is a primary ($1^{\circ}$) amine. It reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to form a sulphonamide containing an acidic hydrogen, which dissolves in alkali. Hence, (A) matches with (IV).

(B) N-methylethanamine ($CH_3NHCH_2CH_3$) is a secondary ($2^{\circ}$) amine. It reacts with Hinsberg's reagent to form a sulphonamide that lacks an acidic hydrogen, making it insoluble in alkali. Hence, (B) matches with (II).

(C) N,N-dimethylmethanamine ($(CH_3)_3N$) is a tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) amine. It does not react with Hinsberg's reagent to form a stable sulphonamide. Hence, (C) matches with (III).

(D) Benzenesulphonyl chloride ($C_6H_5SO_2Cl$) is known as Hinsberg's reagent. Hence, (D) matches with (I).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Reduction of methyl isocyanide with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields a secondary amine, whereas reduction of ethanenitrile yields a primary amine.

Reason (R): In methyl isocyanide, the carbon atom of the isocyano group is directly attached to the methyl group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: Reduction of methyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{NC}$) with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields N-methylmethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{NHCH}_3$), which is a secondary amine. Reduction of ethanenitrile ($\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$) yields ethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$), which is a primary amine.

Reason (R) is false: In isocyanides ($\text{R-NC}$), the nitrogen atom is directly bonded to the alkyl group, not the carbon atom. The carbon atom is at the terminal position. Because the nitrogen is bonded to two carbon atoms (the alkyl carbon and the isocyano carbon), its reduction leads to a secondary amine.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List IList II
A. Primary aliphatic amine + $\text{HNO}_2$I. Yields alcohol and $\text{N}_2$ gas
B. Primary aromatic amine + $\text{HNO}_2$ at $273-278\text{ K}$II. Forms a stable diazonium salt
C. Arenediazonium salt + warming with waterIII. Yields phenol and $\text{N}_2$ gas

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$) to form highly unstable aliphatic diazonium salts, which immediately decompose to yield alcohols and nitrogen gas. (A-I)

Primary aromatic amines react with $\text{HNO}_2$ at low temperatures ($273-278\text{ K}$) to form arenediazonium salts, which are stable under these conditions due to resonance. (B-II)

When an arenediazonium salt solution is warmed with water, it undergoes hydrolysis to yield phenol and nitrogen gas. (C-III)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-I, B-II, C-III.

Answer: A-I, B-II, C-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions does not yield a primary amine as the major product?
questions.solution:
Reduction of amides ($\text{R-CONH}_2$) with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields primary amines. Thus, propanamide gives propan-1-amine.

Reduction of nitriles ($\text{R-CN}$) with $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$ yields primary amines. Thus, ethanenitrile gives ethanamine.

Reduction of nitroalkanes ($\text{R-NO}_2$) with $\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}$ yields primary amines. Thus, nitroethane gives ethanamine.

Reduction of isocyanides (isonitriles, $\text{R-NC}$) with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields secondary amines containing an $-\text{NHCH}_3$ group. Thus, methyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{NC}$) yields N-methylmethanamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{NHCH}_3$), which is a secondary amine.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{NC} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Compound $\mathrm{A}$ having molecular formula $\mathrm{C_3H_7NO}$ is treated with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ in the presence of aqueous $\mathrm{KOH}$ to give compound $\mathrm{B}$. Compound $\mathrm{B}$ is further heated with chloroform and alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ to produce compound $\mathrm{C}$. The compound $\mathrm{C}$ is :
questions.solution:
Compound $\mathrm{A}$ with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_3H_7NO}$ is propanamide ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CONH_2}$).

When propanamide is treated with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ and aqueous $\mathrm{KOH}$, it undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation. This is a step-down reaction where the carbonyl carbon is lost, yielding ethanamine ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$) as compound $\mathrm{B}$.

Heating a primary amine like ethanamine with chloroform ($\mathrm{CHCl_3}$) and alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ results in the Carbylamine reaction. This produces an isocyanide with a highly unpleasant odour. Thus, ethanamine is converted to ethyl isocyanide ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NC}$) as compound $\mathrm{C}$.

Propyl isocyanide and propyl cyanide are incorrect because they do not account for the loss of one carbon atom during the Hoffmann bromamide degradation. Ethyl cyanide is incorrect because the Carbylamine reaction yields an isocyanide, not a cyanide.

Answer: Ethyl isocyanide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction:
I. The reaction is applicable for the preparation of both primary and secondary amines.
II. The amine formed contains one carbon atom less than that present in the parent amide.
III. It involves the migration of an alkyl or aryl group from the carbonyl carbon to the nitrogen atom.
IV. Four moles of NaOH and one mole of B$r_2$ are consumed per mole of the amide.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect because the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction is used for the preparation of primary amines only.

Statement II is correct as the carbonyl carbon of the amide is lost as a carbonate ion, resulting in an amine with one carbon atom less than the parent amide.

Statement III is correct because the reaction mechanism involves the migration of an alkyl or aryl group from the carbonyl carbon to the electron-deficient nitrogen atom.

Statement IV is correct as per the balanced chemical equation for the reaction:
R-CONH_2$ + Br_2$ + 4NaOH → R-NH_2$ + Na_2$CO_3$ + 2NaBr + 2H_2$O

Thus, exactly three statements (II, III, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Only three

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following reaction sequence:
$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{KCN}} X \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} Y \xrightarrow[\text{alc. KOH}]{\text{CHCl}_3, \ \Delta} Z$

The chemical formula of the final product $Z$ is:
questions.solution:
Chloromethane undergoes nucleophilic substitution with $\text{KCN}$ to form ethanenitrile ($X$), which steps up the carbon chain by one carbon atom.

$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{KCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CN} \ (X) + \text{KCl}$

Reduction of ethanenitrile with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields ethanamine ($Y$).

$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 \ (Y)$

Heating ethanamine (a primary amine) with chloroform and alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ results in the Carbylamine reaction, producing ethyl isocyanide ($Z$).

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{KOH} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC} \ (Z) + 3\text{KCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Thus, the final product $Z$ is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$.

$\text{CH}_3\text{NC}$ is incorrect because it fails to account for the carbon chain step-up from $\text{KCN}$. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$ is incorrect as it represents an unreduced nitrile. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_3$ is a secondary amine, not the product of the Carbylamine test.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the molecule 4-amino-$N$-(2-aminoethyl)benzamide, which contains three distinct nitrogen atoms labelled as follows:
(a) The nitrogen of the terminal aliphatic primary amine group
(b) The nitrogen of the amide group
(c) The nitrogen of the aromatic primary amine group

What is the correct decreasing order of basic strength of these labelled nitrogen atoms?
questions.solution:
The basicity of a nitrogen atom depends on the availability of its lone pair for protonation.

Nitrogen (a) belongs to an aliphatic primary amine. Its lone pair is localized and its electron density is increased by the +I effect of the alkyl chain, making it the most basic site.

Nitrogen (c) belongs to an aromatic primary amine (aniline derivative). Its lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring via resonance, making it less basic than the aliphatic amine.

Nitrogen (b) belongs to an amide group. Its lone pair is strongly delocalized onto the highly electronegative carbonyl oxygen atom via resonance. This makes the amide nitrogen the least basic of the three.

Therefore, the correct decreasing order of basic strength is (a) > (c) > (b).

Answer: (a) > (c) > (b)

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Aniline cannot be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.
Reason (R): Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide under ordinary conditions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for the preparation of aliphatic primary amines. Aniline (an aromatic primary amine) cannot be prepared by this method because the synthesis requires the nucleophilic substitution of a halide by the phthalimide anion.

Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution reactions easily under ordinary conditions due to the partial double bond character of the $\text{C}-\text{X}$ bond. Thus, the phthalimide anion cannot attack the aryl halide to form $N$-phenylphthalimide.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

(B)Acetamide(II)Very weak base; lone pair delocalized over oxygen
(C)Diethylamine(III)Secondary aliphatic amine; stronger base than primary in aqueous medium
(D)Aniline(IV)Weaker base than ammonia due to resonance with benzene ring


Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
(A) Guanidine is a very strong base because protonation yields the guanidinium ion, which is stabilized by three equivalent resonance structures, matching with (I).

(B) Acetamide is an amide, making it a very weak base because the nitrogen lone pair is delocalized into the carbonyl group, matching with (II).

(C) Diethylamine is a secondary aliphatic amine, which is a stronger base than primary amines in aqueous medium due to a combination of inductive effect and solvation, matching with (III).

(D) Aniline is an aromatic amine, which is a weaker base than ammonia because the nitrogen lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring, matching with (IV).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A) → (I), (B) → (II), (C) → (III), (D) → (IV).

Answer: (A) → (I), (B) → (II), (C) → (III), (D) → (IV)

questions.q: Methyl isocyanide on reduction with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields compound X. When compound X is treated with Hinsberg's reagent, it forms a product Y. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the nature of product Y?
options: Y is a solid which dissolves in aqueous NaOH.
Y is a solid which dissolves in aqueous HCl.
X does not react with Hinsberg's reagent, hence Y is not formed.
Y is a solid which remains insoluble in aqueous NaOH.
questions.solution:
Reduction of methyl isocyanide ($\text{CH}_3\text{NC}$) with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields dimethylamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{NHCH}_3$), which is a secondary ($2^{\circ}$) amine. This is compound X.

When a secondary amine reacts with Hinsberg's reagent (benzenesulphonyl chloride), it forms an N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide (product Y).

In this case, N,N-dimethylbenzenesulphonamide is formed. Because there is no hydrogen atom attached to the nitrogen atom in this product, it is not acidic and therefore remains insoluble in aqueous alkali (NaOH).

Note: Reduction of alkyl cyanides (nitriles) yields primary amines, whereas reduction of alkyl isocyanides yields secondary amines. A student confusing the two would incorrectly choose the option for a primary amine product.

Answer: Y is a solid which remains insoluble in aqueous NaOH.

questions.solution:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown amine $X$ is treated with nitrous acid ($\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$) at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$. A clear solution is obtained without the evolution of nitrogen gas. However, when this solution is warmed to room temperature, brisk effervescence of a colorless gas is observed. The amine $X$ is:
questions.solution:
The reaction of an amine with nitrous acid at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ without the evolution of nitrogen gas indicates the formation of a stable diazonium salt. This is a characteristic property of primary aromatic amines.

When the solution is warmed to room temperature, the arenediazonium salt becomes unstable and decomposes to form phenol, releasing nitrogen gas which causes brisk effervescence.

Aniline is a primary aromatic amine and perfectly exhibits this behavior.

Benzylamine and ethylamine are primary aliphatic amines (the amino group in benzylamine is attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon). They form highly unstable alkyl diazonium salts that evolve nitrogen gas immediately, even at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$.

N-Methylaniline is a secondary aromatic amine. It reacts with nitrous acid to form N-nitroso-N-methylaniline, which separates as a yellow oil, and does not evolve nitrogen gas even upon warming.

Answer: Aniline

Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Reactions)List-II (Characteristics/Products)
(A) Gabriel phthalimide synthesis(I) Yields an amine with one carbon less
(B) Hoffmann bromamide degradation(II) Yields an alcohol and $\text{N}_2$ gas
(C) Carbylamine reaction(III) Produces a foul-smelling compound
(D) Reaction of $1^{\circ}$ aliphatic amine with $\text{HNO}_2$(IV) Prepares only primary aliphatic amines

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis (A) is used exclusively for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines (IV) because secondary and tertiary amines cannot be formed, and aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion.

Hoffmann bromamide degradation (B) involves the treatment of an amide with bromine in an aqueous or ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide, yielding a primary amine with one carbon less than the parent amide (I).

Carbylamine reaction (C) is given only by primary amines (aliphatic and aromatic), which on heating with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide form isocyanides or carbylamines, which are foul-smelling substances (III).

Reaction of primary aliphatic amines with nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$) (D) forms highly unstable aliphatic diazonium salts, which immediately decompose to yield alcohols and liberate nitrogen gas quantitatively (II).

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II)

questions.q: Compound A (a primary aliphatic amine) reacts with $\text{HNO}_2$ at $273\text{ K}$ to give a gas B and an organic compound C. Compound D (a primary aromatic amine) reacts with $\text{HNO}_2$ at $273\text{ K}$ to form a stable salt E. Salt E on warming with water yields an organic compound F. What are the general classes of compounds C and F respectively?
options: C is an alcohol and F is a phenol
C is an alcohol and F is an alcohol
C is an alkane and F is a phenol
C is an alcohol and F is an aryl chloride
questions.solution:
When a primary aliphatic amine (Compound A) reacts with nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$) at $273\text{ K}$, it forms a highly unstable aliphatic diazonium salt that immediately decomposes to yield an alcohol (Compound C) and nitrogen gas (Gas B).

When a primary aromatic amine (Compound D) reacts with $\text{HNO}_2$ at $273\text{ K}$, it undergoes diazotization to form a stable arenediazonium salt (Salt E).

Upon warming with water, the arenediazonium salt (Salt E) undergoes hydrolysis to form a phenol (Compound F) and releases nitrogen gas.

Thus, C is an alcohol and F is a phenol.

Answer: C is an alcohol and F is a phenol

Thus, $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2 \mathrm{NH}$ is most basic.
